findings.claim: The Str8 branch was removed from the string-header writer. Strings of 32..255 UTF-8 bytes now take the Str16 branch and get a 3-byte header (0xDA) instead of 0xD9 + 1 length byte. Every existing user serializing such strings, including string map keys and values, will see different bytes without opting in. The wire bytes are still decodable, but byte-for-byte output, size, hashes and snapshot tests change. The change is unrelated to the analyzer/SuppressSourceGeneration requirement.

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize a string of 40 ASCII chars (and 255 chars) with MessagePackSerializer.Serialize<string> on the base build and the head build. Base starts with 0xD9 0x28 (Str8), head starts with 0xDA 0x00 0x28 (Str16). Also serialize a [MessagePackObject] type with a 40-char string-key name and compare bytes.

findings.claim: On a key-kind mismatch the member is now skipped with `continue` and the diagnostic is still reported. Previously the code fell through and added the member. For generated output, a type that mixes int and string keys (a MsgPack error case) now produces a formatter missing those members instead of including them. Generator snapshots for such inputs change. Behaviour when the generator is unsuppressed was supposed to stay unchanged.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the generator snapshot tests on a [MessagePackObject] class mixing [Key(0)] and [Key("a")] members. Compare the generated formatter on base and head and check for dropped members.

findings.claim: Duplicate keys are now silently deduplicated (first member wins) via ContainsKey guards instead of throwing on Dictionary.Add. The generated formatter changes for types with duplicate [Key] values, and the generator now drops the later member. Whether the duplicate-key diagnostic still fires is not shown in these hunks, so users may lose the error signal.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile a [MessagePackObject] type with two members sharing [Key(0)] (and one with duplicate string keys). Assert the duplicate-key diagnostic (MsgPack006) is still reported and the generator does not crash. Compare with base.
